issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised): S5a's pull moves an unpinned deck crossing onto the arterial's ground course. At a stage k >= 2, S5b routes on the stage's picked boundary, and S5a then lays the trace (§4.1's S5 row, base l. 5049: 'S5a L1: the trace with every arterial crossing on ground part 0 as a gate'). S5a Trace (2) (l. 5946-5948) pulls the boundary within a 40 m band toward 'local ridges, slope breaks', pins gates where arterials cross, and 'an arterial crossing the boundary on a raised deck pins no gate there'. Only a raised way's ramps, stairs and feet and an aqueduct's supports are impassable to the pull. So where the picked boundary crosses an S4 or earlier-S5b viaduct's deck within 40 m of a foot on the valley's rim (the high ground the pull seeks), the pulled trace can cross that arterial on its ground course beyond the foot, with no pin and no gate vertex. S5b already counted it out of c (l. 5997). The texts then disagree. §4.1 makes it a gate (N_k + 1 gates). §4.8 Gates says 'exactly N, by construction' (l. 7729). F-WALL's B-CITY bar says 'main gates = N exactly; 0 non-gate crossings', and its ladder would 'divert excess arterials to the nearest gate as lanes' (l. 9203), against 'S4 and S5b arterials are never trimmed' (l. 6055). *beneath*'s '(a way S5a pins no gate for meets the trace as anywhere on ground part 0)' (l. 2627) does not decide which applies. T110-2 (3)'s own c14 fixture ('the arterial on the deck pinning no gate', l. 18555-18561) is this case, with no bar against the pull. The same holds at every epoch stage.
issues.required_change: §4.4 S5a Trace (2), after 'an arterial crossing the boundary on a raised deck pins no gate there,' add: 'and the pull keeps that crossing beneath its deck — that arterial's ground course beyond each foot of the deck, within the search band, impassable to the pull as the deck's ramps, stairs and feet are — so the pulled trace crosses each arterial as the picked boundary did: on ground part 0 at its pin, or under its deck (§2.7's crossing table, *beneath*), and the stage's gates are its pins (`N_k`, §4.4 S5b),'. Second end, at scope: in §13.2 T110-2 (3), after 'the arterial on the deck pinning no gate and S5b's count read on ground part 0', add '— and a variant whose picked boundary crosses that deck within the pull's search band of the valley's rim, the pulled trace crossing it under the deck and never on its ground course beyond the foot, the stage's gates exactly `N_k`, 0 non-gate crossings'.

issues.claim: A held arch vault in a `vault` span that a wall comes to stand over at an epoch or a regeneration (C-wall-raised x C-raised-lock x V04). V04 §3.11 UC18 (V04 l. 2459) says a locked vault element is held 'against every generator: ... a reconcile or regeneration that would re-lay, collapse or delete it keeps it — at an epoch reported with E_LOCKED's cause'. Round 6 made the reconcile delete 'every arch vault ... over which a wall now stands' (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (3), l. 1713). §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, reads such a span `open` with 'no arch vault in it' (base l. 2640-2645). T-V6-47's bar is '0 arch vaults in a `vault` span under a wall' (V06 l. 4170). Nothing keeps a generated trace off such a span. V06 §3.7.1's footprint-distance rule is excepted inside an under-deck strip (V06 l. 1463-1466), and the pull and the cost field bar only supports, ramps, stairs and feet (l. 2622-2625). So an epoch circuit, a contraction or a regeneration's ring (W3) across an aqueduct whose `vault` span holds a locked arch vault has two outcomes: UC18 keeps the chamber in the band; *beneath* and the bar remove it. The same holds for a chamber seating a declared placement (V04 l. 1720-1724), whose building is held (item 101 R13; §7.2, l. 10810). There the band and setback cover its footprint, against §5.3's 'footprints ∩ (wall band ⊕ setback) = ∅' (l. 9290), and *beneath* removes its chamber. repair-r6-V04 filed this as its one open hand-off, 'left open for a ruling; nothing written for it' (assemble-r6 §2.1). No ruling closes it.
issues.required_change: §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, at *A `vault` span under the wall*, after '...once no band or strip lies there.' add: 'A wall laid after never comes to stand over a `vault` span whose arch vault is held — locked (V04 §3.11 UC18) or seating a declared placement (V04 §3.5.4 (d)). A trace laid by the `EnceinteStrategy`'s pull or cost field (an epoch's circuit and contraction, a regeneration's ring) treats that span's under-deck strip, widened on each side by the wall strips' widths its rows give (§4.8), as impassable. A stretch laid by neither at an epoch is bent locally to cross under the nearest other span. By hand, the wall's dry run returns E_LOCKED for a locked vault (UC18), and for a declared placement the stretch is bent the same way, a fate. So the vault keeps its chamber, and no footprint enters a band or strip.' Ends: (1) V04: UC18, after 'keeps it', add '— no wall laid after coming to stand over it (§2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'; T-V4-80 (i) adds the epoch-circuit case. (2) V06: §3.7.1's 'a standing raised way's under-deck strip, supports, ramps, stairs and feet excepted where the trace meets it' adds '(never a `vault` span whose arch vault is held, §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'. (3) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (4) adds 'an epoch circuit across a standing aqueduct one of whose `vault` spans holds a locked arch vault, and a second run with a declared placement seated in it: the circuit crossing under another span, the vault, its door and the declared building unchanged, 0 arch vaults in a `vault` span under a wall, 0 footprints in a band or setback; and a hand `drawWall` over the locked one returning E_LOCKED'. The adjudicator may instead rule repair-r6-V04's option (a), where the lock yields at an epoch, reported with E_LOCKED's cause; that option still needs the declared-placement case ruled.

issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x barrier closure, item 106): a barrier anchor or a weld vertex inside a raised way's under-deck strip. *beneath* moves every tower out of the strip: '*No gate and no tower in the under-deck strip* — one the wall's law would place there moves to the nearest point clear of it: a tower along the trace (S7's towers beside a trace an aqueduct at S6's end crossed among them, *over the band*)' (base l. 2645-2648). The barrier closure puts a tower at each anchor: §4.4 S5a (1) 'with a tower at each anchor (§4.8)' (l. 5930, item 106 (a)'s words); §4.8 Towers 'at every barrier anchor (item 106 (a))' (l. 7744); `Enceinte.anchors` 'a tower at each (§4.8)' (l. 2255); PreviewResult.anchors 'each anchor tower's point' (l. 16381); T-V6-47's bar 'its stretches end on tower anchors' (V06 l. 4170). An anchor is the stretch's end, so a tower moved along the trace leaves it bare. *over the band* keeps an aqueduct's strip clear only of 'the trace's gates and towers' (l. 2600). At generation an aqueduct at S6's end is solved before S7 lays any tower, and only 'a tower its spacing would place in the strip' is moved (l. 2601-2603). The case is common where one feature is both the closing barrier and the viaduct's reason: a spur town's gorge side closed by the barrier, with an S4 viaduct across that gorge whose under-deck strip covers the rim where stage 1's trace, laid later at S5a, anchors. Builders differ: one moves the anchor's tower inward (against item 106 (a)'s words and the bars), one keeps it under the deck, one re-anchors the stretch.
issues.required_change: §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, after 'a tower along the trace' add: '— never a barrier anchor's or a weld vertex's (item 106 (a), (f); §4.8 *Towers*). A trace laid after a raised way takes no anchor or weld vertex inside its under-deck strip: the `EnceinteStrategy` anchors the stretch at the nearest point of its barrier edge (or enceinte) clear of the strip, and a stretch laid by neither is bent locally there (by hand a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line), so every anchor keeps its tower —'. *over the band*: 'its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates and towers' -> 'its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates and towers, and at generation, before S7 lays them, of its barrier anchors and weld vertices'. Second end, at scope: §13.2 T110-2 (3) adds 'a gorge-side CITY whose S4 viaduct crosses the gorge at the rim where stage 1's open stretch anchors — the stretch anchored on the rim clear of the under-deck strip, its anchor tower standing; and (1)'s aqueduct laid at S6's end with its course near a ring anchor — its strip clear of the anchor'.

issues.claim: An epoch's founding across a drawn or locked wall (C-wall-raised x C-raised-lock at an epoch). V06 §3.19 (5) (V06 l. 2815-2822) solves a founded course with 'Locked, pinned and declared entities, dossier-listed buildings, every other raised way's supports, enceinte towers and gates ... impassable, filtered before any draw'. In the same sentence: 'a course meeting a standing curtain meets it by §2.7's crossing table — an aqueduct *over the band*'. The crossing table's row W2 (a hand `drawWall`) sends a raised way created later to W1·C1, *over the band* 'or V06's founding', with 'nothing of the wall ... written' (base l. 2603, 2686-2690). Every drawn wall is 'locked by default' and every declared entity is held (§7.2, l. 10810-10820). So on a document whose user drew or locked a ring, the readings split. V06's list makes the ring impassable to an epoch aqueduct, which then never finds a course; its terminal lies 'inside the outermost enceinte' (V06 §3.19 (6)), so it waits (`raised.waited`) at every epoch. The table crosses the ring on a span, writing nothing of it. The same list makes a drawn ground way impassable to a founded deck passing over it, while §7.4's raised-way row lets a deck pass over a locked way ('a raised way over a locked way keeps its span `open`', l. 11447). This is a common path: a user who draws the walls and runs epochs at CITY gets no aqueduct from one builder and one from another. VDC6-01 (determinism) is the hand-edit sibling at §7.1's lock row; this is the epoch path, at a different home.
issues.required_change: V06 §3.19 (5): 'Locked, pinned and declared entities, dossier-listed buildings, every other raised way's supports, enceinte towers and gates, and V05's `skyAccessObstacles` (V05 §2.3b) are **impassable**' -> 'Locked, pinned and declared entities, dossier-listed buildings, every other raised way's supports, enceinte towers and gates, and V05's `skyAccessObstacles` (V05 §2.3b) are **impassable** to the course's supports, ramps, stairs and feet and to its clearing ((7)). A course passes over a locked, pinned or declared ground way on a span, as over any way (item 244's clearance), and meets a locked, pinned or declared wall by §2.7's crossing table, as an unlocked one (an aqueduct *over the band*, a road deck *down before the wall*), nothing of either written'. Second end, at scope: §13.2 T110-2 (1)'s founding clause adds 'and the same founding across a ring drawn by hand (locked by its drawing, §7.2), *over the band*, no wait'; V06's T-V6-73 founding clause adds that run.
